matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the Abstract/Introduction conflates zero-shot and few-shot (fine-tuned) improvements, overstating zero-shot transferability. Finding 1 provides detailed evidence that the 33.68% figure is actually few-shot, not zero-shot as claimed.

GT 2 concerns inconsistency in how spatial masking affects POI/road modalities versus independent modality masking in recovery losses. No finding addresses this specific masking logic inconsistency; findings focus on other issues.

GT 3 concerns unusually low standard deviations and possible cherry-picking in variance reporting. Finding 5 discusses trajectory-recovery gain mismatches but does not address the variance/standard deviation integrity issue.

GT 4 concerns lack of transparency about baseline hyperparameter optimization and fine-tuning rigor. No finding explicitly addresses whether baselines were fairly optimized or describes this experimental design bias.

GT 5 identifies the contradiction between Conclusion claims of no-retraining transfer and experimental evidence showing fine-tuning gains. Finding 1 documents the same cross-section inconsistency between abstract/intro zero-shot claims and actual few-shot results.

GT 6 concerns fabricated or incorrectly attributed citations in Related Work (START, Trembr, TrajCL, MMTEC). Finding 8 identifies dual t2vec references but does not address the broader fabrication/misattribution issue.
GT 7 concerns missing privacy/ethical safeguards for GPS trajectory data. No finding addresses ethical oversight, consent, or privacy-preserving procedures.
GT 8 concerns overly promotional rhetoric in Introduction ('eliminates the need to retrain'). No finding specifically identifies this rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction section.

GT 9 concerns insufficient justification for sub-trajectory masking parameters (40% segments, 20% points). No finding addresses the masking parameter selection or its experimental design implications.

GT 10 identifies Section 5.1's exaggeration of zero-shot capability despite fine-tuning evidence. Finding 1 documents the same issue: the abstract/section 5.1 mislabel few-shot gains as zero-shot, overstating zero-shot performance.

GT 11 concerns imprecise definitions in mixture-of-experts gating (constraints, noise distribution, top-K balancing). Finding 6 notes a broken sentence in the gating description but does not address the logical consistency of the formulation itself.

GT 12 concerns the caveat that trajectory recovery has no zero-shot results (due to label space differences) not being reflected consistently in claims. No finding addresses this specific omission or its impact on transferability claims.

GT 13 identifies that Tables 8-10 show no consistent monotonic improvement with denser sampling, contradicting narrative claims. Finding 5 documents that trajectory-recovery transfer gains in Tables 9-10 are not reproducible and contradict stated improvements.
GT 14 concerns Section 4.1.1 referencing a text embedding model by URL only without proper naming/description. No finding addresses this reproducibility issue with the text embedding model citation.

GT 15 concerns key hyperparameters being buried/inconsistent across sections. Finding 2 documents the contradiction between Appendix B.2 (d=128) and Appendix F (d=256 optimal), directly addressing hyperparameter inconsistency and experimental design clarity.
GT 16 concerns mismatched conference years, page numbers, or volume information in references [4] and [38]. No finding addresses bibliographic accuracy issues in the references section.

GT 17 concerns the Limitations section omitting broader ethical issues (bias, fairness, privacy). No finding addresses the narrow scope of the limitations discussion or missing ethical considerations.
